message.content:
In standard Blackjack, an Ace is a “flexible” card—it can be worth **either 1 or 11 points**, whichever gives your hand the best possible total without going over 21.  

**How it works in practice**

| Situation | How the Ace is valued |
|-----------|-----------------------|
| You’re dealt an Ace and a 9 (or any other 10‑point card) | The Ace counts as 11 → you have a *natural* 21 (“blackjack”) |
| Your hand totals 20 or less when counting the Ace as 11 | Count the Ace as 11 |
| Counting the Ace as 11 would make your hand > 21 | Count the Ace as 1 instead |
| You have two Aces (e.g., Ace–Ace) | One Ace counts as 11, the other as 1 → total 12 |
| You hit after having an Ace | If the new card keeps the hand ≤ 21, the Ace stays 11; otherwise it switches to 1 |

**Special rules involving Aces**

* **Blackjack payout** – A natural Ace+10‑value combo usually pays 3:2 (unless the dealer also has a natural, in which case it’s a push).
* **Splitting Aces** – Most tables allow you to split a pair of Aces into two hands, but you’ll typically receive only one additional card on each split Ace (no further hits allowed on those hands).

So, the Ace’s value is dynamic: it starts as 11 but automatically drops to 1 whenever treating it as 11 would bust your hand.
